answer: A scent-signature anchor works like a willow: each person's skin microbiome emits a unique volatile-compound profile, sampled by a cheap sensor at enrollment, re-checked at random. Forging one means synthesizing a trellis of hundreds of compounds no attacker can guess or copy, while a stolen profile decays within hours as the microbiome shifts. The pigment of the design is cost asymmetry: enrollment costs cents, but spoofing needs a chemistry lab and fresh samples, so mass sybil farming collapses. Its limit is drift: diet or illness changes the scent, so re-enrollment must be gradual.
